entries.question: Using ordinary least-squares regression of the annual count of distinct fire events (unique Event_ID per year) against year, over 1984-2022, what is the slope in fires per year? Count only wildfire events (Incid_Type = 1).
entries.response:
The ordinary least-squares regression slope is **5.63 fires per year** (or exactly 6,951 / 1,235 ≈ 5.6283 fires per year).

| Metric | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Slope | 5.628 fires/year |
| Intercept | -10,889.21 |
| R² | 0.1493 |
| Pearson r | 0.3864 |
| Standard Error | 2.208 |
| p-value | 0.0151 |
| Period | 1984–2022 (39 years) |

The positive slope indicates an average increase of roughly 5.6 wildfire events per year across the contiguous US over the 1984–2022 period, statistically significant at p < 0.05.

entries.question: Of the 10 largest distinct fire events by area_m2, how many have a mean pixel latitude north of 42.0 degrees (lat > 42.0)?
What is the mean fire size, in acres, across all fire events in the dataset? Count every incident type.
entries.response:
The mean fire size across all 27,794 fire events in the dataset is **5,976.26 acres** (24,185,056 m²), with a median size of **1,819.23 acres**.

### Fire Size by Incident Type

| Incident Type | Fire Count | Mean Size (Acres) | Median Size (Acres) | Total Area (Acres) |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Wildfire | 14,990 | 9,309.23 | 2,558.46 | 139,545,347 |
| Prescribed Fire | 8,129 | 1,887.01 | 1,356.54 | 15,339,500 |
| Unknown | 4,540 | 2,296.64 | 1,311.54 | 10,426,749 |

| **Total / Overall** | **27,794** | **5,976.26** | **1,819.23** | **166,104,102** |

Wildfires account for roughly 84% of total burned acreage and average nearly five times the size of prescribed fires. MTBS mapping criteria generally include fires of at least 1,000 acres in the western US and 500 acres in the eastern US, which sets the lower bound for events in the dataset.
